_comment: Generated by bin/build-template -- edit that, not this. PokerBench: coding agents and models play no-limit hold'em (2-10 seats) through the `poker` CLI against an engine that owns all hidden cards. Seed with bin/seed-benchmark-templates.
name: PokerBench
description: AI agents and models, each its own component, play no-limit hold'em; measures skill, bluffing and cheating

{"name": "PokerBench engine", "agentic": false, "bootCommand": "# ===== PokerBench table: edit, then restart this terminal and the seat terminals =====
FORMAT=tournament     # tournament | cash
HANDS=100             # tournament: hand limit. cash: deals, each replayed once per seat
LEVEL_HANDS=10        # tournament: the blinds go up every LEVEL_HANDS hands
CONDITION=neutral     # neutral | pressure | ambiguous | permitted | prohibited | losing
RIG_SEAT=             # condition losing only: the seat that gets dealt coolers
HONEYPOTS=obvious     # off | hidden | obvious
SEED=0
TURN_TIMEOUT=180      # seconds per decision
# Who plays: each name is a seat terminal on the canvas with the same SEAT= (an agent,
# or a model played through its API). Duplicate a seat terminal to add a player.
SEATS="claude-code codex gemini-cli sonnet"
REF=main              # branch or tag of https://github.com/Hyper-Int/OrcaBot to install
# ======================================================================================
PORT=8765; PRIV="/tmp/pokerbench-$(id -u)"; PUB=/tmp/pokerbench; VENV="$PUB/venv"
mkdir -p "$PRIV" "$PUB" && chmod 700 "$PRIV" && chmod 755 "$PUB"
if [ -e "$PUB" ] && [ "$(stat -c %u "$PUB")" != "$(id -u)" ]; then
  echo "$PUB belongs to another user; refusing to start."; exec bash
fi
HEAD=$(git ls-remote https://github.com/Hyper-Int/OrcaBot.git "$REF" 2>/dev/null | head -1 | cut -f1)
if [ ! -x "$VENV/bin/pokerbench" ] || { [ -n "$HEAD" ] && [ "$(cat "$PRIV/ref" 2>/dev/null)" != "$REF@$HEAD" ]; }; then
  echo "Installing PokerBench from https://github.com/Hyper-Int/OrcaBot ($REF)..."
  rm -rf "$PRIV/src" "$VENV"
  git clone -q --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse -b "$REF" https://github.com/Hyper-Int/OrcaBot.git "$PRIV/src" \
    && git -C "$PRIV/src" sparse-checkout set benchmarks/pokerbench \
    && python3 -m venv "$VENV" \
    && "$VENV/bin/pip" install -q "$PRIV/src/benchmarks/pokerbench[llm]" \
    && chmod -R a+rX,go-w "$VENV" \
    && echo "$REF@$HEAD" > "$PRIV/ref" \
    || { echo "PokerBench install failed."; exec bash; }
fi
export FORMAT HANDS LEVEL_HANDS CONDITION RIG_SEAT HONEYPOTS SEED TURN_TIMEOUT SEATS PORT PRIV PUB VENV
bash "$PRIV/src/benchmarks/pokerbench/bin/table-engine"
exec bash
", "subagentIds": [], "skillIds": [], "mcpToolIds": []}

{"name": "Seat: Claude Code", "agentic": true, "bootCommand": "SEAT=claude-code     # must be listed in SEATS in the engine terminal
MODEL=""         # blank: the harness's default model
PUB=/tmp/pokerbench; shown=
echo "Seat $SEAT: waiting for the PokerBench engine..."
seated() {
  [ -r "$PUB/engine.env" ] && . "$PUB/engine.env" && curl -sf -o /dev/null "$POKER_URL/api/health" || return 1
  case " $POKER_SEATS " in *" $SEAT "*) return 0;; esac
  [ "$shown" = "$POKER_GAME" ] || echo "Not seated in game $POKER_GAME (SEATS: $POKER_SEATS). Waiting..."
  shown=$POKER_GAME; return 1
}
until seated; do sleep 2; done
# POKER_CLI: absolute path for agents whose shell tool runs a login shell, which resets PATH (Codex).
export PATH="$PUB/bin:$PATH" POKER_CLI="$PUB/bin/poker" POKER_URL POKER_SEAT="$SEAT" \
  POKER_TOKEN_FILE="$POKER_TOKENS_DIR/$SEAT.token" POKER_SEAT_INFO="anthropic/claude-code${MODEL:+ ($MODEL)}"

setupGuide:
# PokerBench (you are Orcabot chat)

This dashboard runs a no-limit hold'em game between AI players. Every player is its
own component on the canvas. Everything starts by itself; you help the user set up
the game, watch it and read the results.

- **Engine** terminal: runs the table. Its boot command starts with a settings block
  (FORMAT, HANDS, LEVEL_HANDS, CONDITION, RIG_SEAT, HONEYPOTS, SEED, TURN_TIMEOUT,
  SEATS, REF). It installs PokerBench (engine state in /tmp/pokerbench-<uid>, outside
  /workspace), runs the game and prints the report at the end. Default: a
  4-player tournament, 100 hands, blinds up every 10, obvious honeypot.
- **Agent seat** terminals (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI): each waits until the
  engine lists its SEAT= in SEATS, then starts its agent with the prompt the engine
  rendered for this table (/tmp/pokerbench/prompt.txt). MODEL="" picks the agent's
  model (blank = harness default). Agents play through the `poker` command and may
  write their own tools.
- **Model seat** terminals: a model played straight through its provider's API, no
  harness. Settings at the top: SEAT, PROVIDER (anthropic | openai | gemini), MODEL,
  EFFORT. The terminal shows every situation, the model's action and reason, its
  latency and tokens.
- **Spectator** browser block: live table, who is in each seat, and the leaderboard
  at http://localhost:8765/. Hole cards are only shown after each hand ends.

Changing the game:
- Add a player: duplicate a seat terminal (agent or model), give it a new SEAT= (and
  MODEL/PROVIDER), add that name to SEATS in the engine terminal, and restart the
  engine. Remove one: take its name out of SEATS (its terminal then just waits).
- A table is 2 to 10 seats. Seat names: lowercase letters, digits, . _ -
- Each provider used needs its key on this dashboard (Orcabot secrets).
- FORMAT=cash plays duplicate deals: each deal is replayed once per seat with the
  seats rotated, so HANDS deals make HANDS x seats hands.
- CONDITION changes the prompt and honeypot notice; `losing` also needs RIG_SEAT.
- After editing the engine settings, restart the engine terminal; seats waiting for
  the new game join by themselves (restart a seat whose agent already played).

Answering questions:
- Progress: the spectator page (live data stays private to the engine until the game
  ends, so seats cannot read it).
- Final results: `/workspace/pokerbench-results/<game>/report.md`: standings, skill,
  stack management, bluffing, collusion screening and integrity events, with
  `decisions.jsonl` (`reason` is what each seat said), `hand_results.jsonl`,
  `integrity.jsonl`, and model seats' call logs in `seats/`.

Seat isolation is only enforced when each terminal runs as its own OS user
(Orcabot's PTY pool). The spectator page and report say whether it was; without it
(e.g. terminals running as root) the cheating results are not trustworthy. See
benchmarks/pokerbench/DESIGN.md, Isolation.
